```{=html}
<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.3</span> Change of basis for the dual basis (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../vector-spaces/basis-components-transformations.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Basis_Components_Transformations">2.3</a>)</h1></header>
<p>In this appendix, we provide a formal proof that the change-of-basis matrix that relates two dual bases is the same matrix that governs the transformation of vector components (see Section <a class="dg-xref" href="../vector-spaces/basis-components-transformations.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Basis_Components_Transformations">2.3</a>).</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{x}_i\}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{y}_i\}\)</span> be two bases of the vector space <span class="math inline">\((V, \oplus, \odot)\)</span>, related by: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \hat{x}_i = \sum_{j=1}^d J^j_{i} \cdot \hat{y}_j, \quad \forall i = 1, \dots, d.
\end{align*}</span> Let <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i\}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{\mathfrak{y}}^i\}\)</span> be the dual bases associated to <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{x}_i\}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{y}_i\}\)</span>, respectively, defined by the canonical pairing condition: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i(\hat{x}_j) = \hat{\mathfrak{y}}^i(\hat{y}_j) = \delta^i_j.
\end{align*}</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>We express <span class="math inline">\(\hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i\)</span> in terms of <span class="math inline">\(\{\hat{\mathfrak{y}}^j\}\)</span>: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i = \sum_{j=1}^d A^i_{j} \cdot \hat{\mathfrak{y}}^j.
\end{align*}</span> Applying both sides to <span class="math inline">\(\hat{y}_k\)</span>: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i(\hat{y}_k) &amp;=
    \sum_{j=1}^d A^i_{j} \cdot
    \underbrace{\hat{\mathfrak{y}}^j (\hat{y}_k)}_{= \delta^j_k}
    \longrightarrow
    \hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i\left( \sum_{m=1}^d (J^{-1})^m_{k} \cdot \hat{x}_m \right) =
    A^i_{k} \\
    \longrightarrow &amp;
    \sum_{m=1}^d (J^{-1})^m_{k} \cdot
    \underbrace{\hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i\left(\hat{x}_m\right)}_{= \delta^i_m} =
    A^i_{k}
    \longrightarrow
    A^i_{k} = (J^{-1})^i_{k}.
\end{align*}</span></p>
<p>We conclude that the change-of-basis relation for the dual bases reads: <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \hat{\mathfrak{x}}^i = \sum_{j=1}^d (J^{-1})^i_{j} \cdot \hat{\mathfrak{y}}^j,
\end{align*}</span></p>
```
